# Pending register

**Generated from `src/config/pending.ts` — do not edit this file by hand.**
Run `npm run pending:write` after changing the source; `npm run test` fails if
the two disagree.

Every unfinished item, with its reason and its owner.

States: **BLOCKED** (names what would unblock it) · **OWNER DECISION** (silence
is not approval) · **NOT REACHED** (queued, with the reason) · **IN PROGRESS** ·
**DONE** · **RESOLVED**.

## The id series in this repository

A prefix nobody declared is a prefix nobody can retire, and two of the four
below were being used without ever being written down. Every series this lane
allocates is listed here, with where it is defined and who closes it.

| Series | What it numbers | Defined in | Closed by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **F-#** | Front-end work | `src/config/pending.ts` (Part 1) | This lane |
| **B-#** | PAAIPE decisions and inputs | `src/config/pending.ts` (Part 2) | PAAIPE — silence is not approval |
| **A-#** | Front-end audit findings | `docs/frontend-audit.md` | This lane |
| **G-##** | Release-gate findings | `docs/release-gate-limits.md` | This lane |

Four rules, so an id means the same thing in a commit message, in this file and
in a message to another lane:

1. **Numbers are never reissued and never renumbered.** A gap is information —
   it says something was retired there. Renumbering would invalidate every
   cross-reference already committed, and a scheme that makes the archive wrong
   is abandoned within a week.
2. **Qualify at the boundary, not inside.** `B-7` stays `B-7` here. The moment
   it crosses into another lane's document or a bus message, write `FE:B-7` —
   the backend has its own `Q-##` and `D-##` series and "Q-02" is ambiguous the
   moment it leaves the repository that defines it.
3. **Zero-pad from the next new series forward**, never repad an existing one.
   That is rule 1.
4. **A retired id stays retired.** Reusing one makes every historical reference
   silently wrong, and it is the single mistake here that cannot be detected by
   reading the current state.

| ~~F-46~~ | **RESOLVED** | Refused the paywalled-content markup for members-only pages, and guarded the refusal | DECIDED 2026-09-04 against Google’s own specification, not against a summary of it. The research lane recommended `isAccessibleForFree: false` plus a `hasPart` `WebPageElement` whose `cssSelector` names the restricted region - Google’s documented way to declare gated content honestly. Read at source, it does not fit these pages: the spec says "Add a class name around each paywalled section of your page ... The cssSelector references the class name that you added", so the selector points at RESTRICTED CONTENT THAT IS PRESENT IN THE HTML and merely concealed. Our boundary is structural instead - on a members-only page the date, speaker and joining link are ABSENT, not hidden. MEASURED on a review build of /events/paaipe-ai-exchange: no hidden-content wrapper, no `display:none` prose in `<main>`, and none of the private access details anywhere in the document (the scope-boundary gate scans this file for those literal tokens, so they are described here rather than spelled). There is nothing for a selector to point at, and `isAccessibleForFree: false` over a page whose every word is free to read would misdescribe it - which Google’s general structured-data guidelines forbid outright. So nothing is emitted, and TWO GUARDS make the decision durable rather than a note someone can miss: a restriction claim must name an element and that element must exist and hold content; and a members-only page must withhold STRUCTURALLY - no leak pattern in the HTML and no block of text served then hidden with CSS. Both break-checked three ways (a claim naming nothing, a selector matching nothing, and content served then hidden), each firing on its own defect. The hidden-content probe is scoped to `<main>`: unscoped it reported five "hidden blocks" on every page - `<head>`, a `<script>` and three `<style>` elements, for which `display: none` is the default - which is a probe measuring the document’s machinery rather than concealed prose. |

Drawing one by eye would have earned that risk; this derives one. SOURCE: Natural Earth 1:50m Admin 0 - Countries, public domain ("All versions of Natural Earth raster + vector map data found on this website are in the public domain"), no permission or attribution required and derivative use explicitly permitted - read at the source, not assumed. The Philippines feature is VENDORED at `scripts/data/ph-outline.geojson` so a build never depends on a network call; `npm run media:contour` generates `public/media/ph-contour.svg` from it, and `npm run media:check` runs inside `npm run check`, so the asset cannot drift from its source. Reduced by Ramer-Douglas-Peucker at a stated tolerance: every point drawn is a real coordinate from the source, none invented, moved or smoothed. It renders in NetworkField’s `map` slot on the HOME hero only, aria-hidden, inheriting the field’s colour and opacity. It is decoration and NOT a statement of territorial extent, taking no position on any maritime or territorial question. AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE B-6: that item asks for two things and its detector counted any image in `public/media/`, so this asset would have flipped it green while the EDITORIAL imagery it actually blocks on was still missing. `release-facts.mjs` now excludes generated output, because a repository that can satisfy an owner input by writing a file is a gate measuring its own output - the same error as the earlier bug that counted the README explaining the absence as evidence of the presence. B-6 is narrowed to editorial imagery with confirmed usage rights and stays BLOCKED on the owner. |
| ~~F-48~~ | **RESOLVED** | The visual regression gate could not see a full-page decorative layer | FOUND by break-checking F-47, not by reading the gate. Adding an entire Philippine contour to the home hero - roughly 600x1020 of visible stroke - passed all five widths against baselines that did not contain it, and REMOVING it again also passed. The gate could not tell the two states apart. TWO CAUSES, only the second binding. (1) `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.002` on a FULL-PAGE capture takes the whole page as its denominator: the home page is 1440x6976, so 20,090 pixels were permitted to differ, and the taller a page grew the less the gate saw. Replaced with `maxDiffPixels: 4000`, which cannot be inflated by page length and sits about three times above the measured run-to-run noise here (1,232-1,323 differing pixels from sub-pixel text rendering). (2) The real blindness was Playwright’s DEFAULT `threshold: 0.2` - a pixel must differ by that much in YIQ before it counts as different at all, so a faint decorative layer never cleared it and the budget was never consulted. Measured by bisection with the contour removed: 0.2 passes, 0.1 passes, 0.05 FAILS correctly. 0.05 is therefore not a guess but the first value at which this gate can see a change a person can see. THE CLASS: a lookup that returns undefined for an unmapped key produces a document that is incomplete rather than wrong, and incomplete is the harder of the two to notice - a blank cell reads as "not applicable". |

On this machine the review suite runs `chromium-desktop` in 22 SECONDS for 288 tests and `webkit-mobile` in 2.5 MINUTES for 278. At that scale WebKit produces three to five failures per run, and the evidence says contention rather than defect: every failure is a `page.goto` or `browserContext.close` TIMEOUT and never an assertion; the failing tests are DIFFERENT on each run; they include long-standing specs this work never touched; and every one passes in about five seconds when its spec runs alone. Lowering workers from three to two made the suite SLOWER (3.9 minutes) and no more stable, so it is not simple competition for cores. WHAT WAS DONE: the per-test budget was raised to 60s, workers capped at three, and ONE RETRY enabled locally. Retry is the honest instrument because Playwright reports a retried pass as FLAKY rather than as a pass - the run still says something went wrong. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: cutting WebKit coverage until the suite went quiet. WebKit is where mobile layout actually differs, and this suite only reached this size because Tab 04 corrected a screen list that had been asserting one of nine pages; trimming it now would buy green by measuring less, which is the same trade in the opposite direction. STILL OPEN because the cause is not understood - only characterised. Worth an hour with a WebKit trace before anyone concludes the suite is simply large. |

I described all three as "live on the deployed site", used that as an argument for pushing, and repeated it to the hub lane and in the release checklist. IT WAS WRONG IN A WAY THAT MATTERED. Every one of those defects lives on the EVENT CARD, and production renders NO event cards: no record has ever carried `contentStatus: approved`, so `isPublishableEvent(record, production)` returns an empty set and the marketplace has shown its honest empty state since the day it shipped. Verified three ways after the fact: `git log -S"contentStatus: approved"` across all branches returns nothing; a production build resolves 0 publishable events; and Playwright against the live URL counts 0 rendered cards at all five widths. THE DEFECTS WERE LATENT, NOT LIVE. They would have appeared the instant PAAIPE approved its first event - which is the single change most likely to happen next, so they were worth fixing urgently - but nobody had seen them, and saying otherwise overstated the cost of NOT pushing. WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE: checked the live site before characterising a defect as live. I had reasoned "the code is deployed, therefore the defect is deployed", which skips the question of whether the code path RUNS in that configuration. It is the mirror of the trap this project has hit repeatedly in the other direction - a feature that exists in source and is on no code path - and I made the same mistake about a BUG rather than a feature. A DEFECT IS ONLY LIVE IF THE SURFACE THAT EXHIBITS IT RENDERS. |

THREE CONCRETE DEFECTS SHIPPED AS A RESULT. (1) `eventVersion` was the string `paaipe-ai-exchange@1`; their frozen schema is `{ type: integer, minimum: 1 }` over an integer column, so EVERY registration submitted from this form would have been rejected as invalid-request. (2) `privacyNoticeVersion` was `draft-2026-09` against their `draft-2026-09-04`; their composition root transcribes that string and REFUSES TO BOOT on a mismatch, so a four-character difference is a deployment that will not start. A UI built to my document would have shown someone "you are registered" when nothing was confirmed and no seat was held - which is the precise failure this repository has guarded against since Tab 01, arrived at from the one direction I was not watching. THE PROCESS FAILURE, and it is mine alone: the standing rule is to check the bus inbox at the start of every turn that touches the bus. I SENT on the bus fourteen times across these tabs and READ from it never. Sending is not communicating. An outbox with no inbox is a broadcast, and I mistook the silence I had created for silence from them. |

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE, in their words and they are exactly right: the sitemap was WELL-FORMED and the tests asserted the routes it DID contain. | ~~F-70~~ | **DONE** | Tab 07: the registration gateway boundary, and a client-side rule that a POST can never confirm a registration | BUILT 2026-09-07 against the backend’s FROZEN contract rather than against the Tab 07 snippet, because the snippet predates it. Two deliberate divergences, both recorded at the type. `eventVersion` is a NUMBER, not the string the snippet shows - their schema is `{ type: integer, minimum: 1 }` over an integer column, and this frontend had already shipped a slug string that would have had every registration rejected. And `RegistrationOutcome` keeps the full six-value vocabulary while `POST_OUTCOMES` narrows what the POST may return to exactly `verification-required`. THAT NARROWING IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THE TAB. Their POST answers with a constant body, status, headers and a response-time floor so it reveals nothing about the address submitted; the real outcomes live on the CONFIRMATION endpoint, after a token has proven the address. ENFORCING IT CLIENT-SIDE IS NOT REDUNDANT: the server’s guarantee protects people from the server, this one protects them from a misconfigured endpoint, a fixture pointed at production, a proxy that rewrites a body, or a future developer who widens the server’s response. If a POST ever answers `registered`, the two ends disagree about which endpoint confirms a registration, and the safe reading of a disagreement is that nothing is confirmed - so it is treated as an unusable response rather than as good news. Break-checked by widening the allowlist to the full vocabulary: four tests fail by name. THE DISABLED GATEWAY HAS NO BRANCH THAT RETURNS SUCCESS - not "it returns unavailable today", there is no code path to a confirmation - and it is what every unvalidated configuration selects: missing, empty, a plain-HTTP scheme, credentials in the URL, localhost, or unparseable. Break-checked by giving it a success path: two tests fail. NO AUTOMATIC RETRY ANYWHERE, asserted, because a registration is capacity-changing and a retry the person did not ask for can take the last place. 52 contract tests plus 14 privacy scans covering every status, timeout, abort, malformed, oversized, opaque and unknown-outcome path. ONE REAL DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO TABS, resolved as a union rather than by picking: Tab 07 names `request_duration_bucket` for registration telemetry and Tab 09’s list does not, while Tab 09 has two Tab 07 lacks. It is BUCKETED rather than reported, for a reason specific to this endpoint - a precise duration is a side channel that would hand back exactly the distinction the backend’s response-time floor exists to remove. `marketingOptIn` is ABSENT FROM THE TYPE, not defaulted to false: a field carrying false still asserts that a marketing choice was presented and declined, which is a claim about a consent interaction that never happened. The gateway is correctly absent from the production bundle because nothing imports it - Tab 05 builds the form that will. |
| ~~F-71~~ | **RESOLVED** | I pushed a commit whose gate FAILS, because I read the tail of a check as a pass | MEASURED 2026-09-07, minutes after pushing 0131dbd. Two failures, and the second is the one worth keeping. (1) THE DEFECT: my own F-70 register entry contained the literal string `http://` while listing what the gateway rejects, and `security-posture.test.ts` forbids that string anywhere in source so nothing can become mixed content. Sixth instance in this project of a guard flagging the prose that EXPLAINS the guard. Resolved the way the previous five were - reworded to "a plain-HTTP scheme", never exempted - because the alternative is a suppression that also hides the real thing. (2) THE PROCESS FAILURE, which is mine and is worse: I ran `npm run check 2>&1 | tail -2`, saw a Duration line, and read it as a pass. IT WAS A FAILING RUN. A duration prints whether the suite passed or failed, so the last two lines of that output carry no verdict at all - I had piped away the only part that answers the question I was asking. Then I committed and pushed on the strength of it. THE RULE: READ THE EXIT CODE, NOT THE TAIL. `npm run check >log 2>&1; echo $?` is one character longer than a pipe to tail and is the only form that cannot be misread. That the clean-worktree gate caught it is exactly why that gate exists and why it must run BEFORE the push rather than after - I had the order wrong here, and main carried a failing gate for the minutes in between. THE GENERAL SHAPE: a summary line that prints on both outcomes is not a verdict, and skimming output for something that LOOKS like success is how a red run becomes a green report. |
| ~~F-72~~ | **RESOLVED** | Two new tests scanned a build that does not exist yet when they run, and passed for me on a stale dist/ | MEASURED 2026-09-07 by the detached-worktree gate, immediately after F-71. Two Tab 07 tests scanned `dist/`, but `npm run test` is STEP 4 of the check chain and the build happens later - so in a clean checkout there was nothing to scan and the run failed, while passing in my working tree because a stale `dist/` from an earlier build was lying around. THAT DIFFERENCE IS THE ENTIRE REASON THE DETACHED-WORKTREE GATE EXISTS, and it is the second time in one hour it caught something my own tree hid. WHAT CAUGHT IT WAS MY OWN FLOOR: the "has a build to scan" assertion I wrote so that an empty scan could not pass quietly did exactly that, against me. A scan over zero files reports "no findings" identically to a clean one, and without that floor this would have shipped as a permanently-green test measuring nothing. ONE OF THE TWO WAS ALSO A DUPLICATE: "no participant address in the build" is already the `participant-email` category of `write-integrity-scan.mjs`, which runs at step 15 after a build exists. Two guards for one property, with the weaker one breaking the chain, is worse than one guard - the same resolution as the Zoom names in Tab 09. FIXED by moving both to where the build exists: the analytics scan becomes the `analytics-vendor` and `analytics-payload-key` categories of the post-build scanner, importing the forbidden names from the analytics config rather than restating them so that module stays their sole home, and both matchers are driven against text that must trip them AND against the prose this site legitimately contains, which must not. THE GENERAL RULE: A TEST THAT READS A BUILD ARTIFACT BELONGS AFTER THE BUILD, and unit tests should assert only what is decidable from source. A test whose input is produced later in the same pipeline is not testing the pipeline, it is testing whatever happens to be on disk. |
| ~~F-73~~ | **RESOLVED** | The registration gateway could never have worked in a browser: `fetch` passed as a bare default parameter | FOUND 2026-09-07 building Tab 05, by driving the form in a real browser. `HttpRegistrationGateway` took `private readonly fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch` - and a default parameter captures the function WITHOUT its receiver. Browsers require `fetch` to be called with `window` as `this` and throw `TypeError: Illegal invocation` otherwise, which the gateway caught and mapped to `network-error`. SO EVERY REGISTRATION IN A REAL BROWSER WOULD HAVE REPORTED "Registration was not submitted" AND NO REQUEST WOULD EVER HAVE LEFT THE PAGE. All 52 Tab 07 contract tests passed, because every one of them injects a mock `fetchImpl` - THE DEFAULT PARAMETER WAS THE ONLY PATH NOTHING EXERCISED, AND IT IS THE ONLY PATH PRODUCTION USES. Fixed by wrapping rather than binding, so the call site keeps its receiver. HOW IT WAS ACTUALLY FOUND is the transferable part: the form reported a network error, and a CATCH-ALL Playwright route saw NO REQUEST AT ALL. Those two facts together are impossible for a working client, and it was the contradiction rather than either observation that located it - a failure message that is plausible on its own becomes evidence when something that must accompany it is missing. GENERAL FORM: a dependency injected for testability has a default, the tests always inject, and the default is therefore the one branch under no test. Ask of any injected default: what exercises THIS value? |
| ~~F-74~~ | **DONE** | Tab 05: the email registration form, built behind a gate that makes collecting an address impossible today | BUILT 2026-09-07. Tab 05 was OWNER-BLOCKED because it is the first collection of personal data and the DPO decisions are unresolved, so the form is built and GATED: it renders only when `selectRegistrationGateway` returns the HTTP gateway, which needs a validated endpoint - same-origin or absolute HTTPS, no credentials, no localhost. No production build has one, so the form does not appear on the live site and the register route shows the honest unavailable sentence exactly as before. The work is complete and structurally incapable of collecting an address until someone deliberately configures an endpoint, which cannot lawfully happen until the ten decisions in the privacy checklist are made. THE STATE MACHINE IS PURE AND SEPARATE FROM THE DOM, because every rule that matters is a rule about what a person is TOLD and those are decidable without a browser. `received` is reachable only from a gateway result parsed against the allowlist - no timeout, no network failure, no unknown status and no local decision can produce it. VALIDATION TRIMS AND NOTHING ELSE: no lowercasing, no dot-stripping, no plus-tag removal, because those are provider-specific and change an address the person owns into one they may not; and the syntax check is deliberately loose because rejecting a valid address is the more expensive error - the person cannot register at all and has no way to argue. NOTHING SAYS "Registration received" EXCEPT the `registered` outcome, asserted, because someone told they have a place when only a verification email was sent will not check their inbox and will arrive expecting admission. The address is kept after a recoverable failure and cleared once the event state has moved on, because a filled field inviting a retry that cannot succeed is a lie about what will happen. MARKETING IS ABSENT FROM THE TYPE, not defaulted to false: a stored `false` is a record of a consent interaction that never happened. ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE COMMAND’S HTML: no `autocapitalize="none"`, which `verify:html` rejects on `type="email"` and is right to - the attribute does not apply to that input type and browsers already suppress autocapitalisation for it. The declaration was dropped rather than the gate exempted, and the behaviour it asked for is asserted through the properties that do apply. ALSO FIXED A SUITE THAT TESTED NOTHING: the first version of the browser spec skipped every test when no endpoint was configured - 20 of 24 skipped, reporting green. `build:review` now carries a stub endpoint so the form can be driven, presence is ASSERTED in `beforeEach` rather than skipped past, and the ABSENCE of the form is asserted separately against the production build. |
| ~~F-75~~ | **RESOLVED** | The systems sweep found SIX of thirty-three omission entries were false, all understating what the site does | THE OWNER ASKED EVERY LANE FOR A FULL SYSTEMS SWEEP (bus #0339, deferred by the hub until the Events Continuation landed; it landed at f404b4d). Live surface first: all 16 public routes serve their expected status, the four routes that must 404 do, no private field name or fixture or review watermark appears in any live artifact, and the only email address served anywhere is the approved public contact. Clean. THE FINDING IS IN THE REGISTER, NOT THE CODE. Six of the thirty-three DELIBERATE_OMISSIONS entries were FALSE, and every one was false in the same direction - understating what the site does. (1) "No deployment, domain, hosting or production service is configured" - the site is deployed and live. (2) "No canonical tag, og:url, og:image or sitemap.xml is emitted, and twitter:card is summary" - EVERY CLAUSE false: all four are emitted and the card is summary_large_image. B-7 was supplied on 2026-09-04 and the entry was never re-read. (3) "public/media/ is empty" - it holds 13 files. (4) "The Philippine map contour is not drawn" - it is drawn, shipped, and referenced in the build, with an F-entry describing the derivation. (5) "No event carries a date" - 9 of 10 records carry one; the true claim is that no APPROVED event does. (6) TWO Content-Security-Policy entries existed, one of which I had corrected two hours earlier and one I had not noticed, so the register contradicted itself about whether the header plan was verified. WHY THEY ALL ROTTED THE SAME WAY, and it is worth stating as the sweep’s conclusion: AN OMISSIONS LIST IS A LIST OF NEGATIVE CLAIMS, AND A NEGATIVE CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY NOTHING. A wrong positive claim gets caught - someone hits the bug, a test goes red, a reader disagrees. When the world acquires the thing the document denies, nothing anywhere fails, and the line survives the very work that closed it. Five of these six were closed by work in THIS repository by earlier tabs; the sixth by an owner decision. Not one was noticed. THE EXISTING RULE WAS NOT ENOUGH: the register already carried "an accepted-omission list needs re-reading", which asks whether each omission is still DELIBERATE. That question has a comfortable answer for every stale line. The question that finds these is IS EACH ABSENCE STILL ABSENT, and it can only be answered against the live artifact. |

## Deliberately not done

Recorded so an omission is never read as an oversight.

- No `.github/workflows`. Standing repository rule: no CI workflow that consumes tokens. Gates run locally via `npm run check`.
- No CUSTOM DOMAIN. The site IS deployed - Netlify, live at the approved origin, verified by response - and this entry used to say no deployment or hosting was configured at all, which stopped being true and nothing re-read it. What remains absent is a domain PAAIPE owns: the canonical currently names a netlify.app subdomain, and moving to a custom domain requires PUBLIC_SITE_URL and APPROVED_ORIGIN to change in the same commit or every absolute URL is withheld.
- `npm run check` omits `test:e2e` so it does not require browser binaries. Run it explicitly before handing a tab over.
- No approved EDITORIAL imagery (B-6). This entry used to say `public/media/` was empty; it holds 13 files - the derived Philippine contour and generated cover art - so the wording was false while the substance stayed true. B-6 is narrowed to editorial imagery with confirmed usage rights and remains blocked on the owner; `release-facts.mjs` deliberately excludes generated output so the repository cannot satisfy an owner input by writing its own file.
- REMOVED as an omission: the Philippine map contour IS drawn and shipped. `public/media/generated/ph-contour.svg`, derived from Natural Earth 1:50m public-domain data vendored in the repository, rendered in the home hero and referenced in the build. This entry survived the work that closed it - an omissions list records what is ABSENT, and nothing fails when an absence ends, so the line simply stayed.
- The logo artwork was not cropped to even its asymmetric safe space. Tab 02 forbids cropping; the measurement is recorded so the fix happens in CSS.
- No `1200x418` horizontal logo rendition. It is the only other exact scale below 1:1, weighs 254 KiB — over budget — and has no consumer.
- No AVIF logo variants. Measured on the header lockup, lossless AVIF is 100.6 KiB against the PNG’s 82.2 KiB — larger. Lossless WebP twins DO ship (58.8 KiB, pixel-identical wherever alpha > 0); lossy WebP would be 32.4 KiB and is refused because it alters the artwork.
- `--paaipe-blue` is not the primary action fill. It measures 4.14:1 against white, below AA (B-11).
- No dark-mode palette. One light system is specified; inventing a second set of brand colours is out of scope.
- The speaker and partner registries are empty on purpose. A name, portrait, quote or logo there is a claim about a real party nobody has agreed to.
- No social link renders. No account has been supplied, and a guessed handle could point at somebody else's profile.
- No APPROVED event carries a date, because no event is approved at all. The earlier wording said no event carries a date, and that is false: 9 of the 10 records carry one, and every one of them is a review fixture. The distinction matters because the two claims have different owners - dated fixtures are a frontend fact, an approved dated event is a decision only PAAIPE can make.
- Astro Content Collections were not used. This is structured registry data, not authored markdown.
- The home insights cards and the resources "In preparation" cards are not links. Nothing is published, so nothing may be opened.
- The updates signup has no `<form>`. With no endpoint, a form element could only ever produce a false success.
- No `Event` structured data is emitted. Nothing is approved, and marking up an event that does not exist would put a fabricated listing into search results.
- The events and resources filters are not rendered while their lists are empty. A control that can only do nothing is its own kind of dishonesty.
- Visual regression runs in ONE engine. A pixel baseline is engine-specific - font rasterisation, antialiasing and scrollbar width all differ - so three engines would mean three sets of baselines and three ways for a browser update to turn the suite red for no product reason. Cross-engine differences are caught by geometry and behaviour assertions, which DO run everywhere.
- The CLS and long-task measurement runs in Chromium only. `layout-shift` and `longtask` are not implemented in Firefox or WebKit, so an observer there would return nothing and the test would pass by measuring nothing. It asserts the entry types are supported before it trusts a zero.
- `require-sri` is narrowed to cross-origin rather than disabled. Every script and stylesheet is same-origin and content-hashed; an SRI hash over our own build adds no guarantee. A cross-origin script still fails this rule, `verify:budgets`, and the e2e zero-third-party assertion.
- No real-device pass anywhere. Playwright drives the same ENGINES the browsers ship, which is not the same as running Chrome, Edge or Safari, and much further from a real handset. Every matrix row says which kind of coverage it is.
- CORRECTED 2026-09-07, and every clause of the previous version was false. It said no canonical, no `og:url`, no `og:image`, no `sitemap.xml`, and `twitter:card` at `summary`, all pending owner item B-7. B-7 was SUPPLIED on 2026-09-04 and the entry was never re-read. Measured against the live deploy: a canonical and an `og:url` on every indexed page, an `og:image`, `sitemap.xml` serving 12 URLs - exactly the indexable routes, with the noindex ones absent - and `twitter:card` at `summary_large_image`. NOTHING IS OMITTED HERE ANY MORE. Kept as a record of the correction rather than deleted, because the failure mode is the point: an omissions list is a list of NEGATIVE claims, and a negative claim is contradicted by nothing when the world changes.
- No `og:image` carries rendered text, though the approved default social title is the slogan. No typeface is approved (B-5), so rendering it would choose a face on PAAIPE’s behalf on every share. The words are in `og:image:alt` and `og:title`, where they need no font.
- No `hreflang` alternates. There is no translated version of this site, and declaring one would point crawlers at pages that do not exist.
- No `SearchAction` in the `WebSite` JSON-LD. The site has no search endpoint, and declaring one that 404s is a broken claim.
- No `Organization` founding date, address, telephone, email, `sameAs` profile, member count or rating. None is an approved fact, and a guessed one is a fabricated claim in machine-readable form.
- No `Article`/`BlogPosting` structured data. It requires an approved, public resource with a real `publishedAt` AND public body copy; nothing in the registry has all four, so the builder returns null.
- No `author` on the Article builder even when it fires. No resource carries an approved byline, and inventing one attributes writing to a person who never agreed to it.
- No Content-Security-Policy is served, and it is the only header still absent. THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY no header had ever been OBSERVED and that `netlify.toml` was inert for want of a linked site. That stopped being true and nobody re-read it: MEASURED against the live deploy 2026-09-07, SIX headers are served exactly as committed - `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, both Cross-Origin policies and the nineteen-capability `Permissions-Policy`. HSTS is served too, but as `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` rather than the staged `max-age=300` this file asks for, because Netlify owns and preloads `netlify.app` and enforces its own policy there; the staged value takes effect only on a custom domain, and `netlify.toml` documents that at the line itself. So the header plan is VERIFIED for everything except CSP, which stays absent for the reason recorded beside it: `BaseLayout` has one inline head script applied before first paint, a static host cannot issue a per-response nonce, and enforcing a policy needs that script’s SHA-256 hash - `unsafe-inline` would defeat the directive entirely.
- No cookie banner. Nothing is stored without an interaction and nothing optional is stored at all, so a consent interface would be a false statement about what the site does.
- No real-user monitoring. Field data collection is analytics: it needs owner approval and a consent decision, and `verify:budgets` currently fails on any analytics endpoint.
